root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `proto_read_attribute_array()` allocates raw storage and re-decodes the probed attribute, it must reject any top-level template element whose `temp.type` carries `CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE`. Recursive attribute arrays are unsupported here, so the second decode must run only when `(temp.type & CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE) == 0`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable parser continues past the first probe with `temp.type = CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE`, so `temp.type & CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE` is non-zero and the raw outer-value re-decode path still executes. The authoritative fixed image reports the same non-zero mask on the original PoC but does not execute `outer_attr_redecode`, and the adjacent `top_level_non_array_attr` perturbation shows the protected event executing with the mask cleared to zero.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: Verified by the required assertion's vulnerable/original `violated`, fixed/original `guarded`, and fixed/`top_level_non_array_attr` `genuine` matrix.

nodes.state: Immediately after `attrs[i].pValue = p11_rpc_message_alloc_extra(msg, temp.ulValueLen)`, viewing the raw outer-value bytes as the first nested `CK_ATTRIBUTE` yields `pValue = 0xffffffffffffffff` on the crashing PoC because that allocation was filled with `0xff` bytes.
The first non-array nested serializer dispatch is reached with `attr->pValue` still equal to the carried invalid pointer read from the raw outer-value buffer.
The crashing byte-value sink executes `memcpy(value, &byte_value, sizeof(CK_BYTE))` with `value` still equal to the corrupted nested destination pointer.

edges.relation: The first nested `CK_ATTRIBUTE.pValue` view of the raw outer-value buffer is carried unchanged into the later non-array nested serializer dispatch as `attr->pValue`.
The same nested destination pointer passed as `attr->pValue` to the byte serializer becomes the callee's `value` argument at the crashing `memcpy` sink.
